status_at_registration: Frozen before any retrieval execution; only source acquisition and pure source/scorer integrity checks are permitted before runtime freeze.
purpose: Independent source-extraction holdout against real public project histories, complementing the separately frozen synthetic scale experiment. Official repository files and real release-commit timestamps replace authored conversation contents; questions remain evaluator-authored.
freeze_rules: Commit this protocol, the provenance/source/gold manifest, and the evaluator before the first recall call. Root records the resulting exact protocol commit and saves it remotely.

Complete and freeze the runtime candidate before revealing any holdout retrieval outcome to its optimizer. The evaluator agent must not optimize runtime source or disclose query/gold details to the runtime optimizer before the candidate is fixed.

Run both baseline and candidate from exact committed runtime checkouts with identical inputs, budgets and segmentation settings. Bind every tracked runtime file and the actual imported backend/native binary before and after the matrix.
Any result used for further tuning becomes development evidence. Preserve the first attempt and use new unseen public sources/questions for an independent claim about a subsequently tuned candidate.

Do not remove or rewrite a question, gold source span, missing-field label, budget, or evaluator expectation after seeing a retrieval response. Corrections require a new separately identified protocol and retain all old evidence.
segmentation_boundary: The actual runtime supports turn, adaptive, and session; it has no fixed segmentation mode. Each file is one original message/turn, so turn and session are separate interface checks over the same underlying page grouping, not independent quality samples.
ingestion_order: All 10 sources sorted by official commit timestamp, then repository and file path; use MemoryBook.ingest only. One shared database per segmentation mode contains all four project namespaces and both releases of each project.

retrieval.scope: Exact project only; no chapter or session filter is passed. Current versus relevance is explicitly frozen per question; tags/file paths may be present in the query and authentic session metadata.

matrix.source_followup_reads: Read every returned page and every additional conflict-reference page using the same exact project scope. Count separately from recall configurations. No evidence credit is granted from the follow-up body unless its span was present in returned context.

scoring.evidence: Gold is an exact half-open Unicode-codepoint interval in a particular original file at a particular fixed commit. A match requires the union of authenticated returned-context source intervals to cover that whole gold interval. Identical text from another project, release, or file never earns credit.
scoring.complete: All required source spans for that question are covered in returned context. Compare multi-source history questions and multi-fact single-source questions separately.
scoring.first_source: Where predeclared, separately report whether the first returned source belongs to the required release/file. This is source selection, not factual-authority inference; a first source without its required span can still be incomplete.
scoring.source_integrity: Validate every original page, project breadcrumb, source/session/turn/message identity, page and turn coordinates, exact source slices, timestamps, citation framing, excerpt gaps, and character/result budgets. Every conflict page must also belong to the exact query project.
scoring.missing: The named field is absent from all selected source files in that project. Report nonempty context and assessment statuses; neither an empty response nor no_comparable_declaration alone establishes calibrated abstention. Do not infer absence from the rest of the repository.
scoring.regression: Compare each individual gold-span presence and first-source expectation. Unchanged aggregate counts do not excuse an old passing span/case becoming a failure. Retain API and source-integrity errors in all denominators.

acceptance.required: No source-coordinate, project-isolation, budget, or run-identity violations. No formerly returned required span or predeclared first-source success lost versus the registered v0.13 baseline.
acceptance.completeness: Report absolute candidate completeness as well as paired nonregression. Finishing all calls or preserving baseline failures is not a claim that all questions are answered.
acceptance.limits: This holdout establishes only performance on the fixed public-source extraction questions. It is not a production query sample, a coding-LLM evaluation, a cross-product comparison, a timing benchmark or a universal correctness guarantee.
acceptance.project_execution: Report actual project-route count separately from requested project mode. This small corpus is expected to use project-local ranking for every candidate_project call; a disclosed global fallback is never counted as a successful measurement of the project feature.

retention.attempts: Every run requires a new nonexisting output directory; preserve failed and incomplete attempts. Raw API responses and all source page follow-ups are appended before the next query, then losslessly gzip-compressed with both raw and compressed SHA-256 hashes.
outputs: per-mode ingest receipts and SQLite archive snapshots
retention.offline_audit: The saved-record auditor recomputes all source coverage, exact closed-matrix inventories and summary denominators without importing MemoryBook or making new retrieval calls.

python scripts/evaluate_v014_public_holdout.py run --source CANDIDATE_CHECKOUT --commit FROZEN_CANDIDATE_SHA --protocol-commit FROZEN_PROTOCOL_SHA --backend python --arm candidate --ranking-scope global --output NEW_CANDIDATE_GLOBAL_ATTEMPT

python scripts/evaluate_v014_public_holdout.py run --source CANDIDATE_CHECKOUT --commit FROZEN_CANDIDATE_SHA --protocol-commit FROZEN_PROTOCOL_SHA --backend python --arm candidate --ranking-scope project --output NEW_CANDIDATE_PROJECT_ATTEMPT
Repeat all three configurations with --backend native after building and verifying each selected checkout's own extension.

pre_execution_addenda.reason: Root requested explicit constructor ranking_scope selection before any holdout retrieval. The candidate feature is opt-in; default/global compatibility must be evaluated separately.

baseline_global.constructor: Omit ranking_scope; this preserves compatibility with the frozen v0.13 constructor. A missing book.ranking_scope attribute is permitted only for this legacy arm.

candidate_global.constructor: Omit ranking_scope and verify the actual candidate book.ranking_scope is global. This explicitly checks the new runtime's default behavior.

candidate_project.constructor: Pass ranking_scope=project and verify actual book.ranking_scope. Each original response must disclose requested and actual ranking_scope; all global fallbacks and reasons are retained, not counted as project execution.

ranking_binding: Bind requested scope and constructor invocation to report, raw rows, journal, worker arguments, and per-mode observed constructor state. The offline auditor rejects mixed labels and validates the actual response route; a project request that falls back to global is reported explicitly. Within-candidate scope comparisons require one identical runtime commit.
